name: Polyphony
medium: Colored pencil on paper with integrated LED lights, wooden frame, and printed music
description: Music is a highly individual way of expression that connects people of different cultures across different times, building a collective experience for all of us. I’d like to pay tribute to this transcending experience of music using my pencils. It fascinates me that as a violinist, my instrument not only allows me to express myself, but also takes a deep dive into the history of music. Through the lineage of great composers around the world, their ideas transformed music by blending innovative thoughts into a rich cultural melting pot. I am honored to explore this ever-evolving art form, from the timeless genius of Bach in the Baroque era, to Beethoven’s groundbreaking visions in the Classic period, to the cultural flair of Romantic composers like Sarasate, and finally to the bold fusions of minority voices such as Coleridge-Taylor and Esmail. Although none of these music giants share the cultural background as me, their voices resonate within me and inspire me to build music of my own generation. We are in a world with access to so much music, the ability to harness the wisdom of the past, yet a shorter attention span for great music. Inspired by artists before us, how will we, as new musicians from a variety of backgrounds, leverage the powerful technology of today to contribute our own voice to this collective human experience?

name: Where Strings Make Common Ground
medium: Oil, acrylic, and chalk pastel on canvas
description: This painting is a tribute to American Composer Samuel Barber's Violin Concerto. Through my own interpretation of this timeless piece, I further explored how music transcends human experiences. Through Barber's pastoral and introspective melody, I can not only feel the flowing and harmonic terraces of my own homeland of China, but also the rustic and warm tones of the American countryside.

name: Prelude, Adagio, Finale
description: Classical music tells a story. Through my violin, I’ve discovered German composer Max Bruch, whose works are rooted in the emotional depth of German Romanticism. Inspired by classical German statues, I interpret his Violin Concerto as a three-movement tale of Before, Between, and Beyond. The prelude depicts silent struggle, reflecting internalized tension in militaristic Germany of the late 1800s, embodied by a contemplative figure. Between, the music unfolds and rises, as he confronts reality, reaching upward with sentiment like a fallen angel. In the finale, golden forms emerge, as music guides the violinist beyond struggle towards hope and monumental relief.

name: Prokofiev Through the Looking-Glass
medium: Acrylic and chalk pastel on canvas with reflective paper
description: This painting is a tribute to Sergei Prokofiev, an iconic modernist composer's piece, Violin Concerto No.1. The piece on the reflects upon the surreal and dream-like atmosphere of the violin concerto, which is visualized through various organic forms.

name: Saint Saëns' Aquarium
description: Music transcends time, language, and cultural differences, allowing people to look inside themselves, and connect through our common feelings towards our experiences, like nature. As a musician, I always hope to visualize these feelings from music through my art and to add my contribution through my own lens. This work is inspired by "Aquarium", a late 19th-century Romantic music piece by Charles-Camille Saint-Saëns. Although Saint Saens is 200 years older than me, I can clearly see through his eyes a mysterious deep ocean with swarms of ghostly jellyfish and shimmering schools of unknown fish. Every time I hear this music, I am inspired to go outside and see these amazing sights for myself by going to an aquarium or even scuba diving. I feel mesmerized when I use my own imagination to visualize the mysterious yet beautiful deep-ocean scenery that Saint Saens depicted. I chose to use colored pencils to highlight wave shapes that both symbolize the precise harmonies in Saint Saens' music, and ocean waves that the mysterious sea creatures call home. By blending sound waves with ocean waves, I want to add to Saint Saens' message the context of my generation, which is the tsunami of technology advancements that have huge impacts on ocean life. Although I am familiar with realistic illustrations with colored pencils, this is the first time I experimented using this medium to convey abstract forms and ideas. I learned how creative work, like art and music, connects generations together to reflect on our deepest emotions, and inspires us to engage with nature to form our unique bonds with nature. We can all leverage music as an instrument to reflect on our relationship with nature and go outside to experience nature ourselves.

name: Sibelius Violin Concerto
medium: Oil and acrylic on canvas, used violin strings
description: Inspired by Sibelius' Violin Concerto. This painting illustrates the Nordic landscape of Sibelius' composition.

name: Vision of Bowfin
medium: Colored pencil and graphite on paper
description: 2023 is a hostile year for the human race, with many geopolitical conflicts and ongoing wars. This picture was my mental image of my recent visit to USS Bowfin, a World War II submarine at Pearl Harbor. In stark contrast to its colorful and lively tropical surroundings, the submarine is a dismal and monochrome piece of metal evoking the poignant human history of World War II. During the tour, I glanced through a massive door inside the passageway and saw empty shelves where lethal weapons like torpedoes could have been stored. My brain instantly erased this dull and regrettable image of the shelves, and filled in the dark void with a vibrant school of fish, beside which this Bowfin could have swum. This school of fish, each with different coats and appearances, made me think of the people from diverse countries and cultures that live in our world today. I hope that we, like all of these fish, can swim together towards a common goal to make this world a colorful, inclusive, and peaceful place that we call home.

name: Everlasting Flare
medium: Colored pencil on paper, pen on toned paper
description: This scene depicts a late-night stroll in the mountain village of Jiufen, Taiwan. A teenage boy walks along an illuminated street that was once bustling with tourists. On this empty and surreal evening, he ponders his aspirations and dreams, writing them down on a sky lantern. With a gentle lift, he releases the lantern into the dark night sky, filling the winding alleyway with a warm, enduring glow, and sending his dreams on an everlasting journey into the unknown.

name: Out of the Blue
description: On a chilly and quiet morning, I stopped by a vast lagoon on the Northern California coastline during a road trip to take a short break. I was immediately overtaken by the tranquil landscape. Stony shores surrounded a sapphire colored lagoon, while lofty redwoods roamed amongst misty mountains. Out of the blue, a lone kayaker’s paddle broke the motionless water, leaving a trail of glittering ripples. With no one else around, me and the man on the neon colored kayak felt like the only people in the world. I quickly took out my phone to memorialize this once-in-a-lifetime moment.
